defect.title: vacuity-check's blind-mutation pass examines non-tests and mis-reads Swift idiom; 7 of 7 sampled findings are false positives
defect.detail:
Measured 2026-08-21 against test-campaign 0.9.2 on app/Tests. The pass reports examined=1661 mutating=320 blind=88. Two structural errors and two idiom errors inflate that number.

STRUCTURAL. (1) It scans every `func`, not every test. Restricted to swift-testing's own discriminator (a func whose nearest preceding annotation is @Test) the denominator is 1531, not 1661: 130 of the examined functions are not tests. (2) Its helper exclusion at vacuity-check.py:162 is file-scoped — a name is a helper only if called more than once in the file that declares it. A shared stub declared in TestSupport.swift and called from other files therefore reads as a test, so MemoryFileSystem's `write`, `removeItem` and `moveItem`, HTTPStub's `stop` and WatchTestSupport's `remove` are each counted as a blind test. 21 of the 88 are support-file functions.

IDIOM, on the mutator side. (3) The lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` cannot exclude a dot, so a Swift enum case constructor matches a mutator verb: `ServerRowAction.forServer(s, pendingAuth: nil) == .reset(.clearPlacard)` reports ServerPresentationTests::trippedOutranksHeld as mutating via 'reset', where `.reset` is the expected VALUE inside the assertion. 41 of 72 re-measured findings are dot-prefixed. (4) It takes the last mutator by source POSITION and calls everything after it the tail, which misreads three Swift constructs: a mutator inside the assertion (`await #expect(throws: Never.self) { try await store.delete() }` — nothing can follow it by construction), a mutator in a `defer` block (source-early, execution-last, so the whole test body reads as 'after'), and a mutator as the last statement of a loop body whose observation is the next iteration (CallbackLifecycleTests::stopReleasesTheSocket rebinds the port ten times; the read of cycle N is the start() of cycle N+1).

SAMPLE. Of the 15 findings with zero assertions after the last mutator — the highest-yield stratum — 9 were read in full. Two (DiscoveryTests::servers, CapabilityPlateTests::install) are helpers. All 7 remaining are real tests that do observe after mutating, through idioms no reader verb names: `client.calls.last?.operation`, `seen.filter { ... }`, a rebind that throws. Precision on that stratum is 0 of 7.

ARMED, two ways, evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log. A probe @Test that mutates and never observes was added and removed: blind moved 88 -> 89 -> 88 and examined/mutating moved by exactly 1 each time. The check does bite; it is the false-positive rate that is at issue, not the sensitivity.

NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY. The reader side is deliberately loose because a false reader match suppresses a finding. Adding this codebase's read idioms (`calls`, `operation`, `filter`) would lower the number without improving what the pass knows, and the terms are generic enough to suppress true findings too. The 88 stands recorded as a worklist with its measured precision beside it rather than tuned to look better.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 by G22, which declared `testRoot` and gave this pass a corpus for the first time. THE 88 DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Vendored 0.9.2 over `app/Tests` today reports examined=2133 mutating=3 blind=3, against the 1661/320/88 above. The denominator moving up while `mutating` collapses 320 → 3 is not tree churn: 0.9.1 and 0.9.2 ship IDENTICAL DEFAULT_MUTATORS and DEFAULT_READERS, and neither list holds `reset`, `write`, `removeItem`, `moveItem` or `remove` — the verbs this entry's idiom argument turns on. So the 2026-08-21 sitting ran an expanded vocabulary passed on the command line, and `campaign.json` declares none, which makes 88 a figure no documented invocation returns. Its cited evidence, `evidence/arming/blind-mutation.arming.log`, has never existed on any branch of this repository (`git log --all -- '*blind-mutation*'` is empty), so the arming claim above is not checkable from the tree. The measured structural and idiom errors are not withdrawn; what is withdrawn is the population they were measured over.

TODAY'S POPULATION, AND ITS PRECISION. With `testRoot: app` the pass reports examined=2179 mutating=3 re-read-after=0 blind=3, and 0.15.0 returns the same three findings from the same corpus. All THREE were read in full — 3 of 3, not a sample — and all three are false positives. Precision 0 of 3.

A FOURTH CAUSE, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL ENTRY, AND THE ONE THAT PRODUCES TWO OF THE THREE. The body slice is `src[pos:end]` where `pos` is the start of the DECLARATION, so a test whose own name begins with a mutator verb matches itself. `WatchRestartTests::restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite` and `::restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands` contain no mutating call at all: the only `restart\w*\(` in each is `func restart…(` on its own declaration line. Both then read — `WatchWorld.read(scratch.logPath)`, `WatchState.load(path:)`, `WatchWorld.serverNames(in:)` — and assert on `state.mcpServersHash` and `state.restartPending`. The third, `PhoneStorageFailureTests::restartRechecksTheCamera`, does call `await model.restart()` and then asserts twice, on `model.step` and on `model.entry.characters`: property reads that no reader verb names, which is cause (4)'s shape rather than a new one. This cause survives into 0.15.0 unchanged.

NOT ENROLLED IN A GATE, and `blindVocabulary` still not declared, for the reason the entry already gives. A related gap measured at the same sitting: pointed at `src/` — the TypeScript tree, which has no tests — the pass prints `corpus: … (0 file(s))` and `examined=0 mutating=0 blind=0` and contributes nothing to `--gate`. It reports its empty corpus and does not fail on it, so a mis-declared `testRoot` reads as a clean pass.

VOCABULARY DECLARED 2026-08-29 by K4, and the entry's own 'NOT REMEDIED BY VOCABULARY' paragraph is narrowed rather than withdrawn. That paragraph reasons entirely from the READER side, and on the reader side it is still right: adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows, which is why the declared reader list stops short of `expect` and `require` -- swift-testing's assertion macros, 5781 and 383 occurrences, either of which would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero while the pass learned nothing.

THE MUTATOR SIDE WAS NEVER ARGUED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE PASS WAS BLIND. Measured over the same 2282 test bodies at `83e5380`: the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites; a camelCase list derived from this corpus finds 481. So `blind=3` was a reading of 3 of 481, a recall of 0.6%, and the entry's `precision 0 of 3` was a precision over a population the instrument could barely see. `campaign.json` now carries `blindVocabulary` with `only: true`, 19 mutators and 34 readers, derived mechanically -- a verb is kept only where method calls on a receiver are at least half its corpus sites and its own `func` declaration lines at most a quarter, which is causes (3) and (4) of this entry turned into a selection rule.

THE THREE FINDINGS ARE ADJUDICATED, and each clears for a different checkable reason rather than all three for one. `restartIsIssuedBeforeTheStagingWrite`: one fitted mutator, `WatchWorld.remove(scratch)` inside a `defer`, and four declared readers after it -- `load`, `read`, `parse`, `servers`. NOT blind, positively. `restartIsOwedBeforeTheWriteLands`: three fitted mutators, the last `WatchState(restartPending: true).save(`, with `load` after it. NOT blind, positively. `restartRechecksTheCamera`: ZERO fitted mutator call sites in its body. It was flagged only because `restart` is a shipped default and this entry's fourth cause -- the body slice beginning at the declaration -- made `func restartRechecksTheCamera(` match itself. `restart` fails the selection rule (1 method call against 3 declaration lines, of 5 sites), so it is not in the vocabulary and the finding is withdrawn. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN: its real mutation `await model.restart()` is now invisible to the pass, and its reads are still the property comparisons `model.step` and `model.entry.characters` that no reader verb names. It is UNEXAMINED by this instrument, not clean, and that is this entry's ceiling stated once more rather than closed.

ARMED, AND ENROLLED, which the entry recorded as missing. `planning/test-campaign/bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` runs on every `make lint`: two plants identical but for one line, each measured alone and again inside a `shutil.copytree` of the real corpus, requiring examined+1 mutating+1 blind+1 for the blind plant and examined+1 mutating+1 blind+0 for the reading one. The specificity arm is the half a sensitivity arm alone cannot give: a detector that flagged every mutating body would pass the first and say nothing. 6 of 6 as expected on `cache 0.16.0` and again on the `vendor/` pin via `--instrument`. The two disagree only on the denominator -- 2282 against 2277, the five arrow-style `it/test(` blocks 0.9.3 added block detection for -- and agree on blind=111.

THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL PUBLISHES NO BLIND NUMBER. Nothing above touches the structural causes: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a `defer` mutator still reads as source-early -- which is exactly why the first of the three findings above needed reading rather than counting. This entry stays OPEN; what it now carries is a measured recall beside its measured precision.

defect.title: campaign.py's ledger writer prints only cases filed under a surface, silently dropping 8 of 80 — including all four effect-witness cases
defect.detail:
Measured 2026-08-21, test-campaign 0.9.2. `ledger.md`'s header line reads `80 cases` and `73 pass · 3 fail · 0 skip · 4 n/a`; its table carries 72 rows. The eight absent cases are CASE-0145, 0146, 0147, 0148 (lane router-daemon) and CASE-0151, 0152, 0153, 0154 (lane swiftui). All eight pass.

MECHANISM, exact. The writer at campaign.py:1218-1241 buckets every case with `by_surface.setdefault(c.get('surface', '—'), [])`, so a case whose `surface` is absent lands under the literal key `'—'`. It then emits rows with `for s in inventory['surface']: for c in by_surface.get(s['id'], [])`. `'—'` is not a surface id, so that bucket is never visited and its contents are never printed. Nothing warns; the count in the header comes from a different code path than the rows beneath it, which is why the two disagree without either being flagged.

WHAT IS LOST. CASE-0145 through CASE-0148 are this campaign's four `effect-witness` cases — the rung that required building a recorder outside the product, and the most expensive evidence in the run. They are absent from the ledger entirely. A reader of ledger.md cannot learn that the campaign has an effect-witness rung at all.

DIRECTION. The eight dropped are all passes, so the table under-states the work rather than over-stating it. That makes it the safer direction, and it does not make it safe: a reader counting 72 rows against a stated 80 meets an unexplained gap of exactly the kind this campaign is written to make impossible, and the campaign's own rule is that every sweep prints its denominator.

SCOPE. Ledger-specific. evidence.html renders all eight (5 to 11 references each, measured by grep), so the HTML page is correct and only the markdown artifact is affected. Distinct from DEF-052, which is about the defect registry being absent from BOTH artifacts; this one is about cases, in one artifact, via a different mechanism.

defect.title: the macos-glass lane is green over window evidence captured from a pre-M22 build, and four of its cases assert a shell that no longer ships
defect.detail:
Measured 2026-08-27 by G15, while enumerating SURF-025. The committed glass evidence under planning/test-campaign/evidence/ax was last written by commit cef3729 on 20 Aug. M22 then added two destinations and RENUMBERED four accelerators, and nothing re-took the pictures. Running bin/capture-mac-glass.sh against the current build turns four previously-passing cases red, and in every one of them the PRODUCT is right and the recorded evidence is stale:

1. THE MENU MAP. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.swift's selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the pre-M22 map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings the shipped build does not have.

2. SETTINGS IS NOT A SIDEBAR ROW. M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from Destination, and capture-mac-glass.sh still does `axkit select Settings`. That select now fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on Cleanup, and the script photographs the CLEANUP board and files it as SURF-011. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail against it.

THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT BOTH, WHICH IS THE ONE GOOD PART. The capture manifest's readback records that picture as target `app://mac/cleanup` under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename — the exact mechanism the script was rebuilt around. Independently, glass-assert.py --discriminate reports LEAK SURF-007 wrongly accepted 1 of 8 foreign board dumps: SURF-011 — because SURF-011's dump IS the Cleanup board. Two instruments, one cause.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had not grown since it was written. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because the thing it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product.

NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. G15's remit is the Harnesses enumeration, and correcting glass-assert.py's menu map or the Settings navigation would be editing an assertion to restore a green — even though the product is right, that is the move this campaign forbids, and the stale assertion is the instrument that found this. The four cases are set to `fail` with this id in their notes. Owed: re-map SURF-001's menu dict from Destination.selectionDigit, and give SURF-011 a route to the Settings SCENE (Cmd-comma or the app menu) instead of a sidebar select that cannot succeed.

INSTRUMENTED 2026-09-02 (wa5), NOT CLOSED. The cause this row names -- a committed capture carrying no tie to the build it came from -- is now measurable. `planning/test-campaign/bin/glass-build-gate.py` binds every artifact the macos-glass lane cites to the git blob identity of the Mac app's build inputs (the set `scripts/acceptance/build-freshness.sh` compiles from) and exits 2 when that identity is not the one the lane is being read against. It is RED on this tree over all 56 artifacts, in 7 capture groups spanning 20-29 Aug: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.log`. The stamps it reads are marked `reconstructed-from-git` and are deliberately the weaker claim -- git can prove which commit last wrote each artifact, so the record establishes the build the evidence CANNOT BE NEWER THAN rather than the build it was taken from. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh` now calls `glass-build-gate.py --emit` in the run that takes the pictures, stamping from the bundle's own CFBundleShortVersionString/CFBundleVersion and the `.mcprouter-build-stamp` the Makefile writes after `xcodebuild` exits 0, so a re-capture replaces each reconstructed row with a capture-time one. Watched both ways: `evidence/runs/glass-build-gate.selftest.log`, four arms, green over a current capture and red over a stale one, an uncovered one and an undatable row. Case CASE-0342.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. The re-capture itself, which is the whole of what this defect asks for. It needs a macOS host with Xcode and a display server; the work above was done on Windows, where there is no Swift toolchain, no xcodebuild and no way to open the app's window. The four cases stay `fail` with `owed` recording the re-capture and its owner. The second half of the row -- SURF-001's menu map, to be re-read from `Destination.selectionDigit` rather than by hand -- is equally macOS work and equally untouched. Nothing here edits an assertion, a stamp or a recorded identity to restore a green.

defect.title: `Settings` is no longer a sidebar row, so the glass capture filed a neighbouring board's pixels under SURF-011 — and the committed glass evidence predates M22
defect.detail:
Measured 2026-08-27 by G16 while enumerating SURF-026, and independently by G15.

M15 made Settings a Scene and removed the case from `Destination`, and capture-mac-glass.sh still ran `axkit select Settings`. That select fails — `axkit: no sidebar row starting 'Settings'` — the app stays on whichever board the loop visited last, and the shutter filed THAT board's pixels under SURF-011: byte-identical to the Cleanup board on one loop ordering and to the Insights board on another.

THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN INSTRUMENTS CAUGHT IT FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. glass-assert.py's raster uniqueness check went red because two cases shared a sha256; `--discriminate` reported the neighbouring board's predicate wrongly accepting SURF-011's dump, because that dump IS the neighbouring board; and the capture manifest's readback recorded the picture's target as the neighbour's route under subject SURF-011, contradicting its own filename.

FIXED HERE, NARROWLY: the capture script now refuses to photograph a select that did not take, and says which board the window is actually showing. That is the script's own standing rule rather than a new one — it already declines to substitute a picture for the pairing sheet and the status item, and its header records the run that filed the Inbox board as SURF-010. The title and the dump are still written from what the app is really showing, so the failure stays visible downstream; what is withheld is the photograph, because a misattributed picture is the one artefact nothing downstream can correct.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately not fixed here:
1. SURF-011 has no route to the Settings SCENE. It needs Cmd-comma or the app menu, not a sidebar select that cannot succeed. CASE-0016 and CASE-0111 fail until it does.
2. THE MENU MAP IS PRE-M22. Committed SURF-001.menu.txt binds Cmd-4 to `Discover`; the running app binds Cmd-4 to `Harnesses`, exactly as Destination.selectionDigit declares (activity 1, servers 2, skills 3, harnesses 4, discover 5, inbox 6, evals 7, cleanup 8, insights 9). glass-assert.py's SURF-001 `menu` dict is the old map, so CASE-0001 asserts five bindings this build does not have. Correcting it is editing an assertion to restore a green, which this campaign forbids — it is owed as its own item, from Destination.selectionDigit rather than by hand.

WHY IT IS THE SAME FINDING AS G14'S, ONE LAYER DOWN. G14 found the surface LIST had stopped growing while the product did. This is the EVIDENCE not having been re-taken since the build moved: the committed glass artefacts were last written on 20 Aug by cef3729, before M22 added two destinations and renumbered four accelerators. In both cases a completeness gate reported clean because what it measured was a stale artefact rather than the product.

CLOSED ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, 2026-08-27 (G21/G29). The frame this defect produced was still published: `inventory.json` gave SURF-011 the shot `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png`, and at `519aebc` those bytes were the Insights board. `capture-lineage.py --gate` reported it UNTIED because the capture step's own row said `target: app://mac/insights` while the filename said SURF-011 -- the manifest was right and the wall was wrong. Two moves, both provable from git. The Insights frame is renamed `evidence/shots/DEF-059.insights-filed-as-SURF-011.png`, keeping every capture-time field, so the defect keeps its exhibit and no filename match can offer it to SURF-011 again. The Settings capture it overwrote is restored to `SURF-011.build.png` from `cef3729`, TOGETHER WITH ITS MANIFEST ROW from the same commit -- the last commit where those bytes and that row agreed (sha 3b5a26ef, `target: app://mac/settings`, readback `Settings`, 2026-08-20T11:32:58Z). Restoring the pair from one commit is a recovery of a capture-time record; restamping the row against the new bytes would have been the manifest-after-the-fact defect. What is NOT closed is the cause: `axkit select Settings` still fails, so the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 and the glass script still declines to take one.

THE CAUSE NOW HAS A READER, 2026-09-02 (wa5). `axkit select Settings` still fails, and the campaign still has no Settings capture newer than 2026-08-20 -- unchanged. What has changed is that the age is no longer invisible: `bin/glass-build-gate.py` reports `evidence/shots/SURF-011.build.png` and `evidence/ax/SURF-011.*` as STALE against the build this tree would produce, so the lane cannot be green over them again without somebody re-taking them. `bin/capture-mac-glass.sh`'s refusal to photograph a select that did not take is the other half and is unchanged. Both halves of the remaining work -- a route to the Settings SCENE, and the re-capture -- are macOS work and are not attempted here.

defect.title: A too-large refusal names the file and the cap but never the capability, so its picture cannot say what it refuses
defect.text: Measured by G17 on 2026-08-27. `CapabilityDocumentSheet`'s titlebar draws the capability's name from the DOCUMENT, so on any `unavailable` state it falls back to the generic word 'Documentation'. Three of the panel's refusals still identify themselves — `noPackageDirectory`, `packageUnreadable` and `notFound` all interpolate the capability into their headline — but `tooLarge`'s headline is '<file> is too large to show here', which names README.md and the 512 KB cap and never the server. So a photograph of that state is tied to the capability it refuses by its manifest row alone, which is the exact dependency the campaign's capture-lineage rule exists to remove. G17 records it rather than waiving it: check G17-L2 counts the frames that cannot corroborate their own row and fails if that set is anything other than this one.

defect.title: The capture-lineage tie pass has no notion of a route template, so a parameterised surface's capture is reported as a wrong subject
defect.text:
DETECTOR DEFECT in test-campaign, measured 2026-08-27 (G29) against the vendored 0.9.2 and the machine's 0.15.0, which carry a byte-identical `tie()`.

SURF-028's route is `app://mac/servers/{server}/document` -- a family of addresses, one per server. `bin/g17-document-flow.sh` rendered its frames against three of them and recorded each target honestly. `tie()` normalises scheme, host, port, query and fragment away and then asks for string equality or a suffix match, so `mac/servers/g17-capability/document` against `mac/servers/{server}/document` fails all three tests and the gate reports UNTIED -- 'the recorded target does not resolve to the subject's route'. Nothing was pointed at the wrong thing. `references/capture-lineage.md` says resolution is 'deliberately loose on the parts a harness legitimately varies'; a `{server}` segment is exactly such a part, and it is the one case the looseness does not cover.

THE FIX BELONGS UPSTREAM, and is not applied here. `vendor/README.md` pins the tree by checksum so the gates can be re-run from a clone, and a `tie()` that behaves one way in this repository and another way everywhere else stops being evidence -- the same reasoning that keeps X7 and X8 open. Referred out of family (gpt-5.6-sol, high effort, 2026-08-27) and it reached the same conclusion independently: patch upstream, cut a release, re-vendor and re-pin, rather than forking the pinned copy. The patch is one function: treat a route segment of the form `{name}`, `:name` or `*` as matching exactly one non-empty target segment, leaving literal segments, the source-file refusal and the normalisation untouched, and leaving the seeded swap red.

WHAT THIS REPOSITORY DID INSTEAD, and why it is not a workaround. The three served frames are published by the FLOW-006 steps that rendered them, each carrying the concrete route its own capture recorded, and SURF-028 publishes none. That is the registry becoming more accurate rather than less: the surface is a template and has no single portrait, while a step is that surface at one address and can name it. Every frame is now filed at the address the channel was pointed at. The detector limit is unchanged and is what this row records.

defect.title: The Skills board's held-update sheet offers no decision — its only control is Done
defect.text:
Measured by J2 on 2026-08-29, by trying to actuate SURF-004's declared controls and finding four with nothing to press. The design of record's capability-delta sheet offers a two-way decision — `Promote 2.3.0` and `Keep 2.2.0`, recorded as `Promote the held update` and `Keep the installed version` in `evidence/design-controls.json` under state `sheet:capability-delta`. `app/Sources/MCPRouterUI/Boards/SkillSheets.swift` declares three buttons and all three are `Button("Done") { board.sheet = nil }`, so the sheet a user opens to decide about a held update can only be dismissed. `SkillsBoardModel` carries no write at all: no promote, no keep, no never-run. Two further declared controls have no counterpart either — `Never run` is a filter chip the design draws and `SkillPresentation.Filter` (`all | held | local | needsAttention`) has no case for, and `Reveal repo in Finder` appears nowhere under `app/Sources/`.

This is the third shape in `references/inert-ui.md` seen from the other side: not a control whose handler does nothing, but a promised control the build never drew, which no amount of testing the build reveals. It surfaced only because the census gave the surface a denominator and J2 tried to fill it — SURF-004 reaches 2 of 21 actuated and the four are recorded in `inventory.json` under `controlsUnactuatable` rather than quietly dropped.

defect.title: A stdio child that starts and then exits is not noticed, so acquisition waits out the whole startup budget
defect.text:
Measured by R27 on 2026-08-29 against the daemon on a scratch home. A server whose command exists and exits immediately (a shell that returns 17) is acquired for the full startupTimeoutMs and then reported as 'did not initialize within Nms': with the budget at 3000ms the probe took 3.15s wall clock. A server whose command does NOT exist fails in 0.01s, because the spawn itself throws. So the cost is specific to a child that spawns and dies, and the reason is that the handshake races connect() against a timer with no third branch for 'the process exited' - nothing watches the child's termination during startup.

NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a boundary rather than effort. The race lives in StdioUpstreamTransport, which is the reference-diffed startup path R2 owns and R4 compares; adding an exit branch would change how this router reports a failure the reference reports differently, which is a parity decision and not a health-check one. R27's own bound is deliberately narrower - probeTimeoutMs covers the tools/list request so that 'the child never started' and 'the child answered too slowly' stay different answers - which means the budget that governs this arm is the upstream's startupTimeoutMs, and that is stated on the record rather than hidden.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: a manual probe of a crash-looping stdio upstream blocks for the default 60s, and the caller has no way to shorten it except by setting that server's startupTimeoutMs. scripts/acceptance/r27-health.sh sets 1500 on its flaky fixture for exactly this reason, and says so.

defect.title: GET /servers discloses every stdio upstream's full argv to an unauthenticated local caller
defect.text:
Found while building R22's redactor, filed rather than fixed. `Describe.row` emits `command` and `args` RAW, and `ControlHandler.gate` reads the token only for POST/DELETE/PATCH, so the complete command line of every stdio upstream is readable by anything that can open the loopback port. The same function is careful in the adjacent case — it emits `envKeys` and `headerKeys` and never a value, with B10's reasoning attached — so argv is the one credential-carrying position on that route that is published whole.

It matters because argv IS a credential channel: `--token=`, `--api-key=` and a connection string with an inline password are ordinary MCP server invocations, and R22 scrubs args for exactly that reason. The exposure predates R22 and is not made worse by it: the bundle's args go through the value scrub, and this route's do not.

NOT FIXED HERE, and the reason is a parity decision rather than effort. `GET /servers` is reference-diffed — `control-servers-get` in planning/parity/surface.tsv, verdict `proven` — so redacting args moves a surface R4 compares byte for byte, and the ungated GET is itself a ported defect this repository records rather than silently repairs. Closing it means changing both routers or declaring a divergence, and that is the owner's call.
defect.source: app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/Describe.swift transportMembers; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlHandler.swift gate; src/control.ts is the reference half

defect.title: The Windows shell self-test never completes: one destination captured, no report after 180 s
defect.found: 2026-09-02, test-campaign phase 0, on the first run of this instrument since it was written
defect.evidence: scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 exits 2 `NOT-RUN: no selftest.json after 180 s`. shell-startup.log records two launches, 08:09:47.250 and 08:13:14.882, each followed by `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing further. Exactly one capture is written, destination-discover.png at 103 KB - a real drawn board - and `discover` is the FIRST entry in DestinationCatalog.All. The process is gone afterwards: Get-Process MCPRouter.Shell returns nothing. Reproduced on a clean rebuild, scripts/windows/build-shell.ps1 exit 0.
defect.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed. Two hypotheses were formed and both were killed by reading the code. (1) A blocking board constructor: SkillsBoard is the second destination and takes a live control client, but its constructor only wires `Loaded += OnLoaded` and issues no call. (2) An unhandled exception in that `async void` handler terminating the process: RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException, but LiveSkillsControlClient already catches HttpRequestException and TaskCanceledException and rethrows them typed. So the crash site is unknown and this defect is `inconclusive` on cause while being measured on effect.
defect.why-it-matters: This is the only channel that can photograph the Windows boards - the agent session is Session 0, a WinUI process started there dies at 0xC000027B before App's constructor, and the interactive task's window station enumerates zero top-level windows so no external capture reaches it. Until this completes, per-destination pixel evidence exists for ONE of ten destinations and every raster claim about the other nine is inconclusive rather than failing.
defect.contradicts: ORCHESTRATOR.md's WIN3 row records `self-test 0 (10/12/44)`. Either that run happened on a tree this one has diverged from, or on a machine state this one lacks - note control.token is absent here, which LiveSkillsControlClient's own documentation says means the router has never run on this machine.
defect.next: Instrument SelfTestDriver to write its report incrementally and log each destination before it navigates, so the next run names the destination it dies on instead of leaving the question open.  ANSWERED 2026-09-02 by the out-of-process lane, which needed no instrumentation of the app at all: the destination it dies on is `skills`, the second in DestinationCatalog.All. See DEF-077. This defect remains open for the reporting half - the self-test still writes no selftest.json - but its `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` is now narrowed to whatever DEF-077 finds.
defect.resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and not by touching the self-test at all. Its cause was DEF-077: the driver walks DestinationCatalog.All in order, `discover` is first and `skills` is second, and Skills terminated the process - so the run died at board two, having written one capture and no report. With the SkillsBoard fragment namespace corrected, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 now exits 0 reporting `destinations walked: 10, appearances forced: 2, captures on disk: 12, no failures reported`, and the twelve PNGs are on disk. The `mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED` this defect carried is answered: there was never a fault in the self-test.

defect.title: WIN22's Action Center toasts cannot fire: nothing in product source raises a notification
defect.found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
defect.evidence: `ToastNotificationManager` has 0 hits in product source. `AppNotification` has 0 - all 26 raw hits are under obj/ and bin/, generated Windows App SDK projection code. The only real `ToastNotification` hits are WIN22's own two files, where it is the type name of a plain record. The item ships NotificationModels.cs (17 lines), NotificationPresentation.cs (22) and a unit test (23), with no XAML and no view.
defect.why-it-matters: The merge subject reads `WIN22: Windows toast notifications for waiting decisions - review-only actions, safe payloads, 621 tests` and the ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 621 tests green, Action Center toast notifications`. The tests pass because they assert that a function building a payload record builds that payload record. No toast can reach the Action Center.
defect.next: Either build the notification path - AppNotificationManager registration, an AppUserModelID, and the COM activator that makes a toast action reach the review sheet - or withdraw the claim from the ledger and the design of record.
defect.resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and the registration it produces is measured by an instrument outside the product. Three files: MCPRouter.Shell.Model/Notifications/ToastPayloadCodec.cs renders the payload to AppNotification XML and reads a click's arguments back; MCPRouter.Shell/Notifications/ToastNotifier.cs claims an explicit AppUserModelID (Fledgeling.MCPRouter.Shell) through SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID and then calls AppNotificationManager.Register(), which for an unpackaged app writes the COM activator; App.OnToastInvoked routes an OpenReviewSheet invocation to SelectDestination(DestinationCatalog.InboxId), which is the review sheet. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the AUMID must be in force before Register writes under it, or the activator lands under an identity derived from the executable's path and every notification becomes unattributable the moment the install directory moves. THE SAFETY RULE IS NOW A PROPERTY OF THE WIRE. ToastSafetyRule says no toast action installs, approves or grants anything directly, and WIN22's test asserted that the sentence contained its own words. ToastPayloadCodec.Parse admits a closed set of two actions and returns null - not a default - for anything else, and a test parses every argument string in the generated document back through that reader and requires each to land in the set. A button added with an install argument fails there whether or not the sentence was updated. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win22-toast-witness.ps1, 4 arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN22/run/witness.json. The writer is the Windows App SDK notification platform inside the shell process; the recorder is HKCU read by PowerShell's registry provider in a different process, with nothing of this repository's between them. It found the AUMID key, a CustomActivator CLSID {388ED0B3-2D79-49E7-927B-0BFE880FC898}, and that CLSID's LocalServer32 naming MCPRouter.Shell.exe with the platform's own ----AppNotificationActivated: argument. BASELINE requires the key to be ABSENT first, so the run is measuring this launch. ARMED: `-ProveRed` points every read at an AUMID nothing registers and requires all three EFFECT arms to break while BASELINE holds. They did - so the reads are keyed on this application's identity and are not finding whatever registration happens to be nearby, which is the specific way a registry check can be vacuous. Evidence at planning/evidence/WIN22/run/witness-armed.json. THE SHELL'S OWN REPORT IS COLLECTED AND GRADED BY NOTHING. `--toast-probe` writes toast-probe.json saying the platform accepted a Show; the witness carries it as `writerSelfReport` with a field saying it is not evidence, because a process reporting its own effect is exactly the shape of claim this defect was about. WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED: that a toast is DRAWN in the Action Center, and that pressing a button re-activates the process through the registered activator. Enumerating the Action Center needs UserNotificationListener, whose capability is only grantable to a packaged app, and this one is WindowsPackageType=None. DEF-082 carries both.

defect.title: WIN19's packaging and distribution ships no package: no manifest of any kind exists
defect.found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
defect.evidence: A repository-wide search for `*.appxmanifest`, `Package.appxmanifest`, any winget manifest and any `*.wxs` returns nothing. The only winget/MSIX strings anywhere are WIN19's own PackagingModels.cs, PackagingPresentation.cs and their test - and their copies inside .worktrees/. The item is 3 source files totalling 67 added lines, with no XAML and no view.
defect.why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 608 tests green, winget and MSIX distribution channel contract, SmartScreen disclosure, clean uninstall rules`. There is no channel, no package and nothing to uninstall. A user cannot install this application by any of the means the item claims to have delivered.
defect.next: Build the MSIX packaging project and the winget manifest, or reclassify the item as a distribution DESIGN and say so in the ledger.
defect.resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and the package is built, deployed and removed by Windows itself inside the lane that measures it. app/windows/packaging/AppxManifest.xml is a real MSIX manifest whose Identity Name and Publisher are PackagingPresentation.PackageIdentity and .PublisherIdentity rather than values chosen again; app/windows/packaging/winget/ holds the three YAML files winget reads (version, defaultLocale, installer); app/windows/packaging/make-placeholder-assets.py generates the three logo PNGs the manifest references, and says in its own docstring that they are placeholders and that design/marketing-src/ holds the real marks. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win19-package-witness.ps1, 12 arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN19/run/witness.json. Four writers and three recorders, none of them the same thing: MakeAppx.exe packs and .NET's ZipArchive reads the OPC container back; `winget validate` is the winget client applying a schema this repository does not own; Add-AppxPackage deploys and Get-AppxPackage reports. THE INSTALL ARM IS THE ONE THAT TURNS A FILE INTO A PACKAGE. A manifest can pack cleanly, validate cleanly and be refused at deployment for a capability, an architecture or a signature, and every static check passes right up to that point. Windows deployed it: PackageFullName=Fledgeling.MCPRouter_0.1.0.0_x64__facmrsw33693e. 'CLEAN UNINSTALL RULES' IS NOW A MEASURED CLAIM RATHER THAN A SENTENCE. UninstallGuidance promises that uninstalling preserves the configuration under %USERPROFILE%\.claude\mcp-router. The lane plants a marker there, installs, removes, and requires BOTH that Get-AppxPackage reports the package gone AND that the marker survives. A promise about what SURVIVES can only be settled by an uninstall that actually ran. ARMED: `-ProveRed` stages a manifest declaring Fledgeling.MCPRouter.WRONG and requires exactly PACK.identity to break. It did - the package packed cleanly, held a well-formed container, carried its payload and passed every other arm. Nothing else in the toolchain notices an identity drift: the package installs perfectly and is a different product. THE FIRST ARMING ATTEMPT FAILED USEFULLY AND IS RECORDED IN THE LANE'S OWN HEADER. It removed the executable from the layout expecting PACK.payload to break; MakeAppx refuses to pack a manifest naming a file the layout does not carry and exits 1. So PACK.payload cannot be armed by removal and is defended by the packer as well - which makes it cheap redundancy rather than the load-bearing arm it was written as, and the header now says so. WHAT THE LANE PUTS BACK. It creates a self-signed certificate in LocalMachine\TrustedPeople so an unsigned developer package can deploy at all, and removes it in a finally block however the run ends, along with the package. Verified after the run: zero Fledgeling.* packages installed, zero witness certificates trusted. A lane that left a trusted publisher behind would have changed what this machine will install. NOT MEASURED, and DEF-083 carries it: nothing publishes the package anywhere. The winget InstallerUrl is a deliberate example.invalid placeholder and the lane asserts that it IS one, because a plausible-looking GitHub release URL would validate, read as finished, and 404 for the first person who ran `winget install`.

defect.title: WIN23's logon-task supervision registers no task: the model describes a mechanism nothing performs
defect.found: 2026-09-02, tailings audit of the WIN fleet
defect.evidence: `TaskService`, `schtasks`, `ServiceBase` and `StartupTask` appear in exactly two files, scripts/windows/run-shell-selftest.ps1 and scripts/windows/uia/run-probe-lane.ps1 - both WIN18/WIN20 harness scripts, neither WIN23's. LifecyclePresentation.cs maps DaemonSupervisionKind.LogonTask to the string `Scheduled Task at user logon (restarts on crash, un-elevated)`. Its test asserts that this function returns that string.
defect.why-it-matters: The ledger row reads `Merged after verify PASS: 625 tests green, interactive user-session lifecycle model, logon task supervision, live reload contract`. Nothing supervises the router on Windows. The assertion behind the claim cannot fail for any reason connected to whether supervision works, which is the shape `warrant`'s cannot-fail scan exists to catch.
defect.next: Either implement the registration - and a case at the effect-witness rung whose recorder is the Windows task scheduler itself - or record the item as a supervision MODEL awaiting an implementer.
defect.resolution: IMPLEMENTED, and measured by an instrument outside the product. app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell.Live/Lifecycle/LogonTaskSupervisor.cs registers the daemon's logon task through schtasks.exe with a Task Scheduler XML document it builds, and reads the registration back by PARSING THE SCHEDULER'S OWN XML rather than by returning the config it was handed. Registration goes through /XML and not /SC ONLOGON for a reason the argv test pins: the flag form cannot express RestartOnFailure at all, so it would have shipped a task that starts the daemon once and never notices it died, under a description promising the opposite. THE EFFECT WITNESS: scripts/windows/win23-logon-task-witness.ps1, eight arms, run 2026-09-02, evidence at planning/evidence/WIN23/run/witness.json. The writer is the product's supervisor driving schtasks.exe; the recorder is Get-ScheduledTask over the Task Scheduler WMI provider - a different API, a different process, and a different vocabulary: the XML says RunLevel LeastPrivilege and the recorder answers RunLevel Limited, and nothing in this repository translates between them. The scheduler also normalised the interval this run asked for, PT60S, to PT1M, which is the plainest available proof that the read did not come back through anything this code wrote. TWO OF THE EIGHT ARMS ARE ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT: BASELINE requires the recorder to report the task absent before registration, without which a leftover task makes every other arm pass over a run that registered nothing; SILENCE requires it to report absence again afterwards, which is what distinguishes a reader from an echo. ARMED: `-ProveRed` registers with RestartOnCrash false and requires EXACTLY EFFECT.restart to break. It did - RestartCount fell to 0 and every other arm held - so the restart assertion is watching the scheduler rather than restating the config, and it is not an arm that reddens on any change whatsoever. Evidence at planning/evidence/WIN23/run/witness-armed.json. Enrolled in scripts/windows/verify.ps1 as a graded row, so it runs rather than waiting to be remembered. WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED, and it is why this fix is narrower than the ledger row it answers: nothing here logs the user out, so the trigger has never been watched to FIRE, and nothing here starts or kills a daemon, so the restart has never been watched to HAPPEN. What is settled is that the registration the product performs produces, in the Windows task scheduler, a task carrying the three properties the product's own UI describes. That was previously unmeasured entirely. DEF-081 carries the remaining two.

defect.title: The Discover detail dialog is unaddressable from the automation plane: no control carries a name
defect.evidence: DiscoverDetailContent.xaml declares no literal Content on any control and no AutomationProperties.Name at all - it is one of only two view files in MCPRouter.Shell/Views with neither (the other is BoardPlaceholder.xaml, which is a placeholder by design).
defect.why-it-matters: UI Automation is the only out-of-process channel this lane has. A surface whose controls carry no name cannot be asserted against by name, so every case on it would stand at `presence` at best. The same tree serves Narrator, so this is an accessibility defect and a measurability defect in one, exactly as WIN20's brief predicted.
defect.next: Closed. Two rungs stand behind it: the live census in shell-lane.ps1 section 3b, and the structural check in MCPRouter.Shell.Tests/ViewAutomationSurfaceTests, which reads the XAML as XML and fails if any x:Named element loses its automation id.
defect.resolution:
FIXED. Every x:Named element in DiscoverDetailContent.xaml now carries an AutomationProperties.AutomationId, and the four containers that publish nothing of their own - the content root, the argv list, the requirements panel and the requirement fields - carry an AutomationProperties.Name as well.

WHY NOT A NAME ON EVERY ELEMENT, which is what this defect's `next` asked for. A TextBlock already publishes its own Text as its accessible name; an AutomationProperties.Name overrides that, so Narrator would read the label `provenance` instead of the provenance, and an assertion by name would read a constant. That is not a hypothetical - the first run of the settings census reported the board INERT for exactly this reason, because the state readout carried a static Name that never moved however the model did. So the addressing is the AutomationId's job and the name stays the value. The defect's requirement - that the surface be addressable from the automation plane - is met by ids; the accessibility half is met by leaving the text elements' own names intact.

MEASURED, out of process, against the live dialog: shell-lane.ps1 section 3b actuates Discover, waits for a store row, opens the detail dialog through the plane and asserts eight controls by id. It found all eight, each publishing a name. Evidence: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-discover-detail.json.

NOT SETTLED: the dialog is only reachable when the registry search returns a row, which needs network. On a host where it does not, that census row reports `unoracled` rather than passing, and the structural rung (app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell.Tests/ViewAutomationSurfaceTests.cs) is what still runs.

defect.title: The Settings board declares one addressable control against a claim of seven sections of toggles
defect.evidence: SettingsBoard.xaml yields exactly one literal control name, `Copy`, under a scan for Button/ToggleSwitch/CheckBox/ComboBox Content plus AutomationProperties.Name. The WIN13 ledger row claims `7 settings sections, Fluent ToggleSwitch controls`. MEASURED 2026-09-02: planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-settings.json, captured after the destination was actuated through the automation plane, so this is the board as a user sees it rather than as the markup declares it.
defect.mechanism: SETTLED 2026-09-02 against the running board, then settled again against the XAML. Both readings were true and neither was complete. The UIA control view held 60 elements and no element whose control TYPE is ToggleSwitch - but a WinUI ToggleSwitch does not publish as one: its automation peer reports AutomationControlType.Button carrying TogglePattern. The eight Buttons in that dump were Minimize, Restore, Close, Close Navigation, `Copy` and THREE ANONYMOUS TOGGLES. So the board had three of the seven sections WIN13 claims, and its three switches were in the tree the whole time, unnamed and therefore unaddressable. The count and the naming were both wrong, which is why the original either/or resolved to neither branch.
defect.next: Closed. The lane regenerates planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/uia-shell-settings.json every run and the census fails if any section, name or toggle state goes missing. Persistence is DEF-087, the Copy handler is DEF-088.
defect.resolution:
FIXED. SettingsBoard.xaml now renders all seven sections SettingsPresentation.SectionOrder declares - Router, Harnesses, Session analyst, Updates, Security, Ambient surface, Advanced - each on a container carrying an AutomationProperties.Name and an AutomationProperties.AutomationId, and its three switches carry the names SettingsPresentation.ToggleLabel declares. The switches are no longer inert: each writes through SettingsBoardModel.UpdateToggle and the board's state readout re-renders from the MODEL, so a switch that stopped writing through would move and leave the readout unmoved.

MEASURED, out of process, by scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 section 3b against the live shell: all 7 sections addressable, all 3 toggles named with a readable toggle state, and TogglePattern.Toggle() on `Launch router daemon at sign-in` moved the readout from `LaunchAtLogin=on - RequireConfirmationOnDestructive=on - ShowAmbientIcon=on` to `LaunchAtLogin=off - ...`. That last read is the one that matters: it is an effect on a DIFFERENT element from the one actuated, taken by a different process.

NOT SETTLED, and deliberately not folded into the green. (1) Nothing PERSISTS a setting. SettingsBoardModel holds state in memory for the life of the board; closing the shell forgets it, and no toggle here reaches the router, the registry or a logon task. The three switches are honest about the model and say nothing about the machine - DEF-087 carries that. (2) Four of the seven sections carry governance prose rather than controls, because this build has no harness settings, no session analyst and no update check; that is WIN13's own design and the sections are addressable so a future control lands in a named place. (3) The `Copy` button is named but its Click is still unhandled - it was unhandled before this change too, and DEF-088 carries it.

defect.title: Selecting the Skills destination terminates MCPRouter.Shell
defect.found: 2026-09-02, the first run of scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 against the real shell
defect.evidence: Reproduced on four consecutive lane runs, each on a freshly launched process. The lane launches MCPRouter.Shell in the interactive session, actuates each pane item through SelectionItemPattern.Select() out of process, and reads the tree back. `discover` selects and renders 55 named elements with the window title 'Discover'. Selecting `skills` ends the process: the window title read comes back empty, the control-view dump holds zero elements, and Get-Process returns nothing for the pid. Windows records it: Application Error 1000, MCPRouter.Shell.exe, exception code 0xC000027B in CoreMessagingXP.dll, with a matching WER APPCRASH bucket. shell-startup.log's last line for the run is `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing after it.
defect.mechanism: PARTLY ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION, the WinRT mechanism for an unhandled exception surfacing out of a XAML callback, which matches SkillsBoard's `private async void OnLoaded(...) => await RefreshAsync();` - an async void handler, where an escaping exception terminates the process rather than faulting a task anybody awaits. What is NOT established is which throw escapes. RefreshAsync catches only SkillsControlException around each await, and LiveSkillsControlClient does convert HttpRequestException, TaskCanceledException, 404, 401 and JsonException into that typed error - so the read path is well guarded and the escaping exception is more likely to come from Render(), which builds XAML fragments by string concatenation and loads them, than from the client. That is a direction to look, not a finding, and it is recorded as such.
defect.why-it-matters: It is the second of ten destinations and it takes the whole application with it, so a user who clicks Skills loses the window. It also explains DEF-071 without replacing it: the in-process self-test captures exactly one board, `destination-discover.png`, and then never writes its report - because `discover` is first in DestinationCatalog.All and `skills` is second, and the process does not survive the second. Two instruments, one in-process and one out-of-process, independently stop at the same boundary.
defect.next: Give OnLoaded a try/catch that renders the failed state instead of terminating, which is the product fix; then find the escaping exception with a first-chance handler or by bisecting Render(). The lane's crash row is the regression test and it is already wired: this defect closes when `skills` reports pass rather than CRASH in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
defect.resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02. Root cause named by the stack the new logging produced: SkillsBoard splices `FragmentNs` into 33 XAML fragments and FragmentNs declared ONLY the default namespace, while the fragments use `x:Name` - so `x:` was an undeclared prefix and XamlReader.Load threw. The first fragment to load is ErrorState's, which is what a board renders when no router is running, so it threw inside `async void OnLoaded` and took the process with it. Two changes: FragmentNs now declares xmlns:x, and OnLoaded catches rather than letting anything escape an async void. VERIFIED: `skills` reports pass on the lane, 57 elements, on a process that survives the whole ten-destination sweep with no relaunch.

defect.title: Three destinations select in the pane and never open their board: Harnesses, Cleanup, Inbox
defect.found: 2026-09-02, scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 driving the real shell through UI Automation
defect.evidence: Selecting Harnesses, Cleanup or Inbox through SelectionItemPattern.Select() leaves the window title, the caption band and the ENTIRE control-view tree byte-identical to the destination before it - the lane's fingerprint over the tree's accessible names is unchanged, which is why it is recorded as a COLLAPSE rather than as an empty board. The pane item itself does take the selection: SelectionItemPattern.Current.IsSelected reads True on all three. So the highlight moves and nothing behind it does. Order-independent: a reverse sweep, where every destination has a different predecessor, fails on exactly the same three. Six others - Discover, Servers, Activity, Checks, Insights, Settings - pass in both directions, so the harness, the actuation and the oracle all work.
defect.mechanism: NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED. ShowDestination assigns `BoardHost.Content = destinationId switch {...}` and only THEN sets BoardTitle.Text and Title. An exception thrown while constructing the board abandons that statement and leaves all three unchanged, which is exactly the observed signature. The three failing boards are also the only three in the tree whose constructors do work beyond InitializeComponent: HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard each call `_model.PopulateSampleData()` and then a Render method, while every passing board either does nothing more or defers to a Loaded handler. That is a strong correlate and it is not proof, so no statement is named here. The app's own diagnostic cannot settle it - see DEF-079.
defect.why-it-matters: This is the inert-shell shape the campaign exists to catch, and it survived every check the fleet ran: the boards compile, the pane draws all ten items with correct names, navigation was reviewed as honest by reading ShowDestination's switch (which is correct - all ten map to distinct board types), and the unit tests cover the models rather than the mounting. Three of nine boards - a third of the product's surface - cannot be opened by a user, and nothing in the repository said so until a harness actuated a control and read a state outside it.
defect.next: Wrap the board construction in ShowDestination so a failing board renders a visible error state instead of silently leaving the previous one up - the silent failure is worse than the crash because it looks like a working application. Then construct HarnessesBoard, CleanupBoard and InboxBoard under a debugger or a first-chance handler to name the throw. This defect closes when all three report pass in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json.
defect.resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02, and the mechanism that was NARROWED, NOT ESTABLISHED is now established - it was the constructor throw, as the correlate suggested, but the throw itself was one shared cause across all three: `SubtleButtonStyle` is not a WinUI 3 resource key and was never defined by this app. Eleven references across five views asked for it. Cleanup and Inbox threw inside InitializeComponent, Harnesses threw in its card builder, and the XAML ones surfaced as `XamlParseException: undeclared prefix`, which names neither the key nor the file. The style is now defined in App.xaml, based on the platform's DefaultButtonStyle. ShowDestination also now catches a failing board and mounts a visible BoardFailure card, so this class of fault can never again leave a working-looking application on screen. VERIFIED: all three report pass with real trees - Harnesses 70, Cleanup 90, Inbox 79 elements - and a mutation run that renames the style key turns exactly those three red again, which proves the lane's new failure-card check rather than its title check is what catches them. NOTE: AmbientFlyoutView and CapabilityDocumentPanel carry the same eleven-reference fault and are fixed by the same definition; neither has been opened by any harness, so both are fixed-but-unverified.

defect.title: The shell's unhandled-exception log never fires, including for a crash that definitely had one
defect.found: 2026-09-02, while trying to use it to diagnose DEF-077 and DEF-078
defect.evidence:
App.xaml.cs registers `UnhandledException += (_, e) => StartupLog.Write($"unhandled: {e.Message}
{e.Exception}")`, whose comment says it is "the only trace a session that cannot see the desktop will ever have". shell-startup.log holds 16 launches across 2026-09-02 and not one `unhandled:` line - including the eight runs in which selecting Skills terminated the process with exception code 0xC000027B, which is by definition an unhandled exception. Every launch logs `launched` and `loaded at rasterization scale 1.5` and nothing else, so the log itself is being written.
defect.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. 0xC000027B is STATUS_STOWED_EXCEPTION raised in CoreMessagingXP.dll, and a stowed exception surfacing below the managed dispatch boundary may terminate the process without the Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException event ever being raised. That would make the handler correct and simply unreachable for this class of failure, which is a different remedy from a broken handler.
defect.why-it-matters: It is the only diagnostic an agent session has for a GUI it cannot see, and its silence reads as `no exception occurred` when it means `nothing was recorded`. That inversion cost real time on DEF-077 and DEF-078: the absence of a log line had to be discounted as evidence before either could be reasoned about honestly.
defect.next: Add AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException beside the XAML handler, and have SkillsBoard's async void OnLoaded log-and-render rather than let an exception escape. Then re-run the lane and require an `unhandled:` line for the Skills crash before this closes - an empty log must stop being indistinguishable from a clean run.
defect.resolution: FIXED 2026-09-02 by measurement rather than by code. The remedy for the handlers themselves landed earlier - AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException registered beside the XAML handler - and this defect stayed open because none of the three had been OBSERVED firing. All three now have been. App.xaml.cs takes `--fault <ui|appdomain|task|dispatcher>`, compiled out outside DEBUG and inert unless passed, which takes one deliberate escape route per kind; scripts/windows/win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 launches the shell once per kind and reads the line each handler wrote back out of shell-startup.log, in a different process, after the process that wrote it exited. OBSERVED FIRING, each with the line it wrote in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/unhandled-witness.json: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application.UnhandledException (`unhandled: [xaml] ...`, for a throw on the UI thread inside XAML's dispatch of OnLaunched); AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException (`unhandled: [appdomain terminating=True] ...`, for a throw on a non-UI foreground thread); and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException (`unhandled: [unobserved-task] ...`, for a faulted task nobody awaits, after a collection and WaitForPendingFinalizers). A BASELINE launch with no --fault wrote no `unhandled:` line, so the flag is inert when absent and the three lines are the injection's; every arm reads only the bytes appended after its own launch, so no line from an earlier run can satisfy one. -ProveRed left the unobserved-task handler unregistered and broke EFFECT.task alone while the other three arms held (unhandled-witness-armed.json). The lane is enrolled as a graded row in scripts/windows/verify.ps1 (exit 0 pass, 3 NO VERDICT, else FAIL) and carried as CASE-0342. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and neither of these is folded into the green above. (1) A throw from a DispatcherQueue callback on the same UI thread reaches NO handler at all: the process disappears having written `fault: injecting` and nothing after it. That is a second silent route and it is DEF-085, filed rather than absorbed here; the witness runs it as an UNGRADED probe so a reader sees it without the lane's verdict depending on it. (2) The original 0xC000027B stowed exception is still not reproduced - the injected UI fault is an ordinary managed exception, not a stowed one raised in CoreMessagingXP - so whether the XAML handler would have caught the Skills crash of 2026-09-02 remains unmeasured. DEF-086 carries it. (3) Fault injection is compiled out outside DEBUG, so this lane grades the Debug binary only.
defect.statusSyncNote: Synced from defects-windows.json, which reckon does not read. The two registers disagreed on this row and only inventory.json reaches the ledger, so a defect closed by a witness lane was still counted as broken. That drift is its own defect and is filed; this is the one row, not the class.

defect.title: WIN23's logon trigger has never been watched to fire, and the restart has never been watched to happen
defect.evidence: scripts/windows/win23-logon-task-witness.ps1 measures the REGISTRATION and says so in its own notMeasured[]: it does not log the user out and it does not start or kill a daemon. So the two behaviours the operator is actually promised - that the daemon comes up at logon, and that a crashed one comes back - rest on the Windows task scheduler honouring a LogonTrigger and a RestartOnFailure block that this repository has confirmed are present and has never confirmed are honoured.
defect.why-it-matters: This is a much smaller claim than DEF-074's was, and it is filed rather than folded into the fix because folding it in is exactly how DEF-074 happened: a narrower thing was measured and a wider thing was reported. Trusting the scheduler to honour its own manifest is a reasonable place to stop; not saying that is where one stopped is not.
defect.next: Either measure it - a lane that starts the registered task, kills the process and watches the scheduler's LastTaskResult and NumberOfMissedRuns move, which needs a real daemon binary this tree does not yet build for Windows - or record the two behaviours as resting on the Windows task scheduler's own contract and close this on that basis.

defect.title: No instrument on this host can see a toast in the Action Center, or a click on one
defect.evidence: scripts/windows/win22-toast-witness.ps1 witnesses the REGISTRATION and says so in its own notMeasured[]. Enumerating what is in the Action Center requires Windows.UI.Notifications.Management.UserNotificationListener, whose userNotificationListener capability is only grantable to a packaged application; MCPRouter.Shell.csproj is WindowsPackageType=None. Nothing here can press a notification button either.
defect.why-it-matters: The two behaviours the operator is promised - a toast appears, and pressing Review opens the review sheet - rest on Windows honouring a registration this repository has confirmed is present. That is a reasonable place to stop. Not saying it is where one stopped is what DEF-072 was, one layer up, so it is filed rather than folded into that fix.
defect.next: It becomes measurable if WIN19's MSIX packaging lands: a packaged build can hold the userNotificationListener capability, and UserNotificationListener.GetNotificationsAsync would then be an independent recorder for the toast itself. So this is downstream of DEF-073 rather than independent of it.

defect.title: The winget manifest points at a placeholder URL because nothing publishes the package
defect.evidence: app/windows/packaging/winget/Fledgeling.MCPRouter.installer.yaml carries InstallerUrl: https://example.invalid/PLACEHOLDER-no-release-is-published/... with zeroed InstallerSha256 and SignatureSha256. scripts/windows/win19-package-witness.ps1 asserts the placeholder is PRESENT rather than that the URL resolves. No release pipeline exists in this repository: nothing builds a signed package, uploads it, or opens a pull request against microsoft/winget-pkgs.
defect.why-it-matters: `winget install Fledgeling.MCPRouter` cannot work, and the manifest validates, so nothing in the toolchain says so. The placeholder is deliberate for exactly that reason - a plausible URL would make this a manifest that looks shipped. What it costs is that the Winget member of DistributionChannel is a contract with a builder behind it and no publisher, which is a smaller gap than DEF-073's and still a gap.
defect.next: Publishing is an outward-facing action nobody has authorised: it needs a code-signing certificate this repository does not hold, a release artifact hosted somewhere, and a pull request into a third-party repository. Route it to the owner rather than closing it here. When it is done, the placeholder assertion in the witness inverts into a resolving-URL check and the two hashes become real.

defect.title: Discover store rows publish their class name as their accessible name
defect.found: 2026-09-02, while proving DEF-075 against the live dialog
defect.evidence: The UIA census in scripts/windows/uia/shell-lane.ps1 opened the Discover detail dialog from a store row whose accessible name read `MCPRouter.Shell.Views.DiscoverRow` - the type's ToString(). Recorded verbatim in planning/evidence/WIN-SHELL/run/assert-report.json under the control row `discover.detail`.

Narrator therefore announces the class name of every entry in the store instead of the capability's own name, and no out-of-process check can address a particular row - the census had to take whichever row was not a navigation label. defect.title: No Windows setting persists, and none of them reaches the machine
defect.evidence: SettingsBoardModel holds RouterSettingsState in memory and has no store: no file, no registry key, no control-API call. The three switches on the Settings board write through to it and nowhere else, so closing the shell forgets every change. `Launch router daemon at sign-in` in particular does not register or remove the logon task that WIN23 builds - it moves a boolean.
defect.why-it-matters: This is the inert-UI failure one layer further along than DEF-076's, and it is the layer the census cannot see: the toggle moves, the model moves, the readout moves, and nothing outside the process changes. A user who turns off launch-at-sign-in has been told something that is not true. Filed separately rather than folded into DEF-076's fix, because DEF-076's green covers the board and the model and must not be read as covering the machine.
defect.next: Decide what each toggle actually owns - the logon task for LaunchAtLogin (WIN23 already registers one), the tray surface for ShowAmbientIcon, a confirmation policy the boards read for RequireConfirmationOnDestructive - then persist the state and give each one an out-of-process witness in its own vocabulary, the way the toast witness reads the registry rather than asking the shell.

defect.title: The Settings board's Copy button is named and does nothing
defect.evidence: SettingsBoard.xaml declares the endpoint Copy button with no Click handler. It was unhandled before DEF-076's fix and still is; the fix gave it an accessible name (`Copy the loopback endpoint`) and an automation id, which makes it addressable and no more functional.
defect.why-it-matters: It was the ONE actuable control the census found on this board, so it is the control most likely to be mistaken for evidence that the board works. Invoking it copies nothing to the clipboard.
defect.next: Wire the Click to a DataPackage carrying RouterSettingsState.Endpoint, then witness it with a clipboard read taken by a process that is not the shell.

defect.title: `actuates` names both a button somebody pressed and an operation a lane called
defect.detail: SURF-045, SURF-046 and SURF-047 declare `controls` that nobody can press - LogonTaskSupervisor.Register, MakeAppx pack, Add-AppxPackage. The census has one word for the thing a case drives, so those eight operations are counted in the same denominator as the Mac Servers board's buttons, and the actuated ratio therefore overstates how much GLASS has been driven by however many of the numerator are operations. The alternative was leaving three shipped surfaces unenumerated so that the count stayed pure, which is the failure the campaign exists to catch, so the surfaces were enumerated and this was written down instead.
defect.resolution: Settled 2026-09-02 by wb4, in three parts. (1) THE POPULATIONS ARE SEPARATE. SURF-045, SURF-046 and SURF-047 declare `operations` / `operationsSource` rather than `controls` / `controlsSource`, and `bin/control-census.py` keys every one of its dictionaries on (kind, surface) so there is no structure in the file whose values span both. It prints `Controls:` and `Operations:` as separate lines, each with its own denominator and its own disposition partition, and says in the output that the two are never added. `message-only` stays a control-side class, because "the whole promised effect is a panel appearing" has no meaning for a call a lane makes. (2) THE FIELD REFUSES A COMMAND. `command_shape()` refuses an invocation-with-arguments -- a path separator between two words, a `-x`/`--xx` flag, a script or assembly extension, a `foo(` call, a shell operator, or a known runner followed by arguments -- wherever it appears, in a case's `actuates` AND in a surface's own declared list. Declaring the command was the laundering route the pre-existing stray check could not see, and that is now the arm that catches it. (3) BOTH REDDEN, planted and reverted; CASE-0396 carries the plants. (4) THE MACHINE THAT WROTE THE COMMAND NO LONGER DOES. `bin/win-cases-from-lane.py` generated `"actuates": ["UIA TogglePattern.Toggle()"]` for every effect row and omitted `actuatesSurface` on all ten destination rows; the last wave's integration pass corrected both by hand in cases.json and the next run of the generator would have written them straight back. It now carries a CONTROL_ACTUATES table binding a lane control id to the control the surface declares - empty by default, because a naming row has driven nothing - and sets `actuatesSurface` to the shell on the destination rows. Measured by running the generator over a copy of `planning/` in a scratch tree and running the census against its output: exit 0, where the same run before this change produced nine stray findings. WHAT MOVED, said plainly because it is a published figure: the headline fell from `57 of 210 declared control(s) actuated ... across 33 surface(s)` to `49 of 202 ... across 30 surface(s)`, 27.1% to 24.3%. Every one of the eight names that left was in the numerator, which is exactly the overstatement this row described; they are now reported as `Operations: 8 of 8 ... across 3 surface(s)`. No case changed and no measurement was withdrawn. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: `command_shape()` cannot tell a bare two-word command name (`winget validate`, `MakeAppx pack`) from an operation name, and the misfiled-shape check only recognises a PascalCase `Foo.Bar`, so SURF-047's four members could be moved back under `controls` without the gate noticing. DEF-131 carries that.

defect.title: The shell's NavigationView pane carries no AutomationProperties.Name
defect.found: 2026-09-02, by win-surface-reconcile.py R4 while grounding SURF-030's control list
defect.evidence: app/windows/MCPRouter.Shell/Shell/ShellWindow.xaml:91 declares the <muxc:NavigationView> with x:Name="Nav" and no AutomationProperties.Name. The ten items INSIDE it are named - ShellWindow.xaml.cs:267 sets each NavigationViewItem's AutomationProperties.Name from DestinationCatalog, and :293 names the pane-footer Settings item - so the omission is the container's alone.
defect.why-it-matters: From the automation plane, and from a screen reader, the pane itself has no name: it is addressable by AutomationId and by control type and by nothing a person would say out loud. It surfaced from the census end rather than from an accessibility sweep - CASE-0334 recorded actuating a control the campaign called "NavigationView pane", a phrase that appears in no source file, because there was no real name to use. A synthesised label in the registry is what a missing accessible name looks like from inside the denominator.
defect.resolution: Not settled. The registry half is done: the control is declared as `Nav`, its x:Name, so its provenance can be checked against ShellWindow.xaml, and win-surface-reconcile.py R4 now refuses any control that appears in no named source. The PRODUCT half is untouched - nobody has added an AutomationProperties.Name to the NavigationView, and this row stays open until somebody does. It is filed rather than fixed here because wa3's scope is the denominator and adding an accessible name is a change to the shell.
defect.renumberNote: Allocated as DEF-084 by a concurrent Wave A runner and renumbered at merge: wa1 had already published a different row under DEF-084. The id is the only thing that changed.

defect.title: defects.in.json and inventory.json disagree about the adjudication of three defect rows, and only one of the two is read
defect.text: FOUND BY ARMING, not by reading. The status remap on this branch first synced `defects.in.json` to `inventory.json` wholesale, and the sync moved three rows that have nothing to do with vocabulary: DEF-002 `open` -> `closed`, DEF-040 `open-instrument` -> `fixed · in-campaign`, DEF-063 `open · measured` -> `open`. Those are adjudications, not spellings, so the sync was reverted and only the six unclassifiable SHAPES were rewritten in place. THE STANDING FACT: `reckon.read_campaign` reads defects from `inventory.json` and from nowhere else, so `defects.in.json` is a hand-edited source that no reckoning reads. Three of its 24 rows say something different from the file that is read, and nothing compares them. A reader who opens the source file gets a different answer about DEF-002, DEF-040 and DEF-063 than the ledger gives. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and why this is open rather than fixed: which of the two files is right about each of the three is an adjudication somebody has to make by reading the defect, and a runner remapping words is the wrong person to make it. `defect-status-vocabulary-gate.py` reads both files, so a NEW unclassifiable word is caught in either; it has no opinion on whether two files that both classify agree with each other.
defect.renumberNote: Allocated as DEF-085 in inventory.json by one Wave A runner while another published a DIFFERENT DEF-085 into defects-windows.json. defect.title: An exception thrown from a DispatcherQueue callback reaches no handler and is never logged
defect.found: 2026-09-02, while proving DEF-079's three handlers fire
defect.evidence: scripts/windows/win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 runs `--fault dispatcher` as an ungraded probe: the shell posts a throwing callback to the ShellWindow's DispatcherQueue and the process disappears. Its region of shell-startup.log ends at `fault: injecting dispatcher` with nothing appended - no `unhandled: [xaml]`, no `unhandled: [appdomain ...]`, no `unhandled: [unobserved-task]`. defect.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. A DispatcherQueue callback is invoked below the XAML framework's own dispatch, so an exception escaping it is not on the path Application.UnhandledException watches, and it is on the UI thread rather than a CLR thread whose escape AppDomain's handler would see. Whether it becomes a stowed exception the way 0xC000027B does is exactly the question DEF-086 cannot answer on this host.
defect.why-it-matters: It is the shape most of the shell's own asynchronous work has. OnToastInvoked routes a toast activation through _window.DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue, and anything that marshals back to the UI thread does the same. A failure there terminates the shell and leaves the log reading exactly as it does after a clean run - which is the inversion DEF-079 was about, arriving by a route DEF-079's fix does not cover.
defect.next: Either wrap the enqueued callbacks the shell posts, so the failure is logged at the site that owns it, or find the framework hook this route does reach. Then turn the ungraded PROBE.dispatcher line in win-shell-unhandled-witness.ps1 into a fourth EFFECT arm - the injection and the reader already exist, and only the grading is withheld.

requirement.text: The router says when an upstream's credential is running out or has been refused, before a tool call fails on it — and it can say that it does not know. Expiry is DERIVED from what the router already holds (`authorizedAt` + `expires_in` in the record it wrote when the flow settled), never asked of the upstream, so nothing is spawned to answer the question. A token whose record declares no lifetime reads `unknown` carrying the reason, and there is no path from a missing number to `valid`. A configured value the router will not take is reported as refused with its scope rather than clamped in silence. Repetition is throttled and escalation is not: a warning becoming an expiry, and an expiry moving because the credential was replaced, go out at once, and re-authorising CLEARS the warning rather than ageing it out.
requirement.provider: app/Sources/RouterCore/AuthExpiry/AuthExpiryRecord.swift derives the state and app/Sources/RouterCore/AuthExpiry/AuthExpiryMonitor.swift holds the throttle; app/Sources/RouterCore/Control/ControlAuthExpiry.swift serves both routes on the loopback control listener bound by RouterService, which is the inbound socket this row names. Witnessed by scripts/acceptance/r26-auth-expiry.sh, which plants credential records on disk in a scratch home, drives the routes over the daemon's own socket, and PAIRS every zero-children reading with a reading that moves when the planted file moves — an absence asserted alone is satisfied by a feature that does nothing.
requirement.note: R26. It inherits R27's rule (REQ-029) and meets it by not needing it: a health probe of a stdio upstream IS a child process, so R27 defaults background probing off and never lets a scheduled sweep cold-start. An expiry needs no probe at all, so this feature arms no task, holds no timer and spawns nothing — which is why it is ON by default where health probing is off. The vacuity rule is `warnWithinMs`'s floor of 60000 with zero REFUSED: at zero a token passes straight from valid to expired, `expiring` is unreachable, and the promise 'you are told before it stops working' would hold only because nothing can enter the state it names. R27's tripAfter floor of 2 is the same rule one item earlier. The `mobbin` lesson is carried into the notification rather than rediscovered: with a refresh token held, no command is offered, because telling its owner to re-authorise sends them round a loop that cannot succeed.
